from.place: The symmetric infinity-operad, inert/active pointed maps, relative operadic algebra categories, and active slices used to state the terminal-active mapping property.

title: Relative symmetric infinity-operadic algebra interfaces
statement: Use the enhanced simplicial-set and cocartesian-fibration conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the generic relative operation mapping spaces and composition graphs of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $\mathrm{Fin}_*$ be the skeleton of finite pointed sets with object $n$ equal to $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ pointed at $0$, and pointed maps as morphisms. Inert maps have exactly one preimage of each non-basepoint; active maps have no non-basepoint mapping to $0$. An inert edge over its nerve is cocartesian over an inert map. A symmetric infinity-operad is an inner fibration to this nerve, with cocartesian inert lifts, the operation-space Segal product decompositions, and a tuple object for each finite family of colors, including the empty family. A map of such operads preserves inert edges and the base. For $v:P\to O$ and $q:E\to O$, define the coherent relative diagram category by requiring the entire diagram simplex to lie over the fixed $v$, and define $\operatorname{Alg}_{P/O}(E)$ as its full inert-preserving subcategory. Restriction along $u:P\to Q$ is actual precomposition in every degree. Define the active slice over a color and its pullback $J_d$ along $u$, with its source object and active-arrow projections. For a restriction functor $R:B\to A$, define the coherent triple category $T$ with objects $(a,b,\eta:a\to Rb)$, retaining the coherent squares and all their higher simplices, its projections $r:T\to A$ and $s:T\to B$, and the identity-triple functor $S:b\mapsto(Rb,b,1)$. The canonical mapping comparison is the span $\operatorname{Map}_B(sH,G)\leftarrow\operatorname{Map}_T(H,SG)\to\operatorname{Map}_A(rH,R G)$ induced by these projections. Its left leg forgets the square, so its inverse followed by the right leg represents $b\mapsto R(b)\eta$. Define its being an equivalence by both specified legs being weak equivalences for every $G$; this coherent span retains naturality in $G$ and contravariantly in triples. Finally define the terminal-active cocone condition: for each color $d$ there is a terminal $t=(p,\alpha:u(p)\to d)$ of $J_d$ and a composition triangle with short edges $\eta_p$ and $F(\alpha)$ whose long edge is $q$-cocartesian.
